links.note: Five sub-questions, and the first two are classification: iron ore as non-renewable and tidal energy as replenishable, i.e. the exhaustibility basis in 23922. The other three reach 23928, 23931 and 23930 one line each. DEFECT: sub-answer (c) gives 'intensive cultivation' as the cause of land degradation in Punjab; the chapter attributes it to over-irrigation causing waterlogging, salinity and alkalinity.

DEFECT FIRST: this row is corrupted - the stem field holds only '1).' and the ANSWER field holds the question ('Explain land use pattern in India and why has the land under forest not increased much since 1960-61'), so the row has no answer at all. On that recovered stem the concept is 23927, the land-use categories including land under forest. The row needs repairing, not re-homing.

How technical and economic development raised resource consumption; the answer argues from Gandhiji on the exploitative nature of modern technology being the root cause of resource depletion. That is 23923. (The stem also carries a stray '2).' prefix from the same split that damaged qid:87372.)
Consequences of oil supplies being exhausted - the depletion that follows unplanned exploitation, 23923. 23922 would fit a question asking how to CLASSIFY oil; this one asks what depletion does.

Six crossword clues, three of which are soil types - black (high water retention), laterite (intensively leached), alluvial (the Great Plains). That majority is 23930. NOTE: the stored answer list has the black and laterite answers in the wrong clue order.
Asks the bases on which resources are classified, keyed to origin - 23922's description names origin, exhaustibility, ownership and status of development as exactly those bases.

National resources (minerals, water, forests, wildlife and land within the political boundary) is the ownership basis of 23922, distinguished from the individual, community and international categories in the distractors.

Sustainable development - development without damaging the environment and without compromising future generations - closes the development-of-resources passage as the answer to the problems 23923 lists. 23924 is the planning strategy, a separate section.

The keyed sentence, 'irrational consumption and over-utilization of resources may lead to socio-economic and environmental problems', is 23923's description. The two distractors C and D are lifted from the resource-planning stages (23924), which makes the discrimination explicit.
Land put to non-agricultural uses (buildings, roads, factories) as the category not available for cultivation is one of 23927's enumerated land-use classes.

India's total geographical area of 3.28 million sq km is the denominator for the land-use table, which the chapter introduces in the same paragraph as the 93-per-cent reporting coverage. 23927. 23926 covers the relief features, not the area total.
Waste land as rocky, arid and desert areas is one of 23927's land-use categories; the distractors are the current and other fallow classes and non-agricultural uses from the same list.

Change in temperature, running water, wind, glaciers and decomposers as the soil-forming forces is the opening of the soil section that 23930 heads. 23931 is the erosion-and-conservation half of that section.
Alluvial as the most widely spread soil in India - a direct claim about the soil types, 23930.
'The processes of soil formation and erosion go on simultaneously and generally there is a balance between the two' is the opening sentence of the soil-erosion section, 23931.

Continues qid:105891 - deforestation, over-grazing, construction and mining disturbing that balance. It sits in the soil-erosion passage (23931) rather than 23928, which is the land-degradation list, although the two name overlapping causes.

The definition of shelter belts as planting lines of trees to create shelter is the soil-conservation passage's wording, so 23931. 23929 also names shelter belts but as one of the arid-area land-degradation remedies; this item asks what they ARE.

Asks what shelter belts contribute, in the same soil-conservation passage as qid:105896, so 23931. DEFECT: the key is marked 'To conserve water'. The chapter says shelter belts contributed significantly to the stabilisation of sand dunes and to stabilising the desert in western India - option C. The key is wrong.

Iron ore as abiotic is the origin basis of 23922. DEFECT: the option set is ambiguous - iron ore is equally non-renewable (option B), which is how qid:87371(a) keys the same substance. Two options are defensible; only the origin one is marked.

Water in dams and forests as a RESERVE usable in future is the status-of-development basis in 23922 (potential, developed, stock, reserve), and the distractor 'potential' is the neighbouring category in that same scheme.
